correctness.rationale: For independently seeded P3, q in (0,1), independent bond transmissibility p in [0,1], S at least one imported seed, read exact RESULT.md and reconstructed all four edge states and eight seed states. In noninfection form, conditional covariance is [z(1-A-B+C)-(1-A)(1-B)]/z^2 with z=1-(1-q)^3. Independent symbolic algebra reproduced z^2 Cov(X0,X1|S)=q^2t^2(1-p)F_t(p) and z^2 Cov(X0,X2|S)=-q^2t^3(1-p)^2[1+2p(1+t)+tp^2]. The published Bernstein-basis formula for F_t prime is strictly positive on p in [0,1], F_t(0)<0<F_t(1), proving a UNIQUE interior adjacent sign threshold, with two-node failure and endpoint strict negativity for p<1. Verified q=1/2 root approximately .218089980704572 and asymptotic boundary coefficients; unconditioned covariance is nonnegative by product-measure positive association. This is a finite-graph exact symbolic proof, not a simulation of all real parameter values.

value.rationale: A minimal three-node counterexample where conditioning changes the sign of an intrinsically positively associated final-infection field, with a rigorously unique transmissibility threshold for adjacent sites and persistent endpoint anticorrelation, is a motivated sharp boundary case. It identifies the first path size permitting reversal and clarifies the hazards of outbreak-selection conditioning. It is valuable as a finite exact test case, not a universal epidemic theorem.

limitations: Exactly three vertices, homogeneous independent seed bits and independent edge openings, final-ever infected only.
Other models with correlated outgoing transmissions or source selection may have different covariance signs.
